props.text: This recipe creates a rich, velvety risotto for 4 people without using dairy. The key to the creamy texture lies in the high starch content of Arborio rice and the agitation process (stirring), which releases that starch into the broth. We will use a mix of mushrooms for depth of flavor and finish with a "mantecatura" technique using vegan fat to emulsify the sauce.

This recipe assumes you have a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven to distribute heat evenly. We assume the use of dry white wine (like Pinot Grigio or Sauvignon Blanc) to deglaze the pan, but you can substitute extra vegetable broth mixed with a teaspoon of lemon juice or white wine vinegar if you prefer an alcohol-free version. We also assume the use of store-bought low-sodium vegetable broth, but homemade stock works excellently.
1.5 cups Arborio rice (do not rinse, as starch is needed)
5 to 6 cups vegetable broth (kept warm in a separate pot)
1 lb mixed mushrooms (cremini, shiitake, oyster), sliced
2 tbsp vegan butter (or extra olive oil)
0.25 cup nutritional yeast (optional, for cheesy flavor)
Salt and black pepper to taste

Pour the vegetable broth into a saucepan and keep it on a low simmer next to your main cooking pot. Cold broth shocks the rice and stops the cooking process, preventing the creamy texture from developing.

In your heavy-bottomed pot, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil over medium-high heat. Add the sliced mushrooms and cook until browned and their liquid has evaporated (about 5-8 minutes). Season with a pinch of salt. Remove mushrooms from the pot and set aside. This prevents them from getting rubbery during the rice cooking.

Reduce heat to medium. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil to the pot. Add shallots and cook until softened (2-3 minutes). Add garlic and thyme, cooking for another minute until fragrant. Add the Arborio rice. Toast the rice, stirring constantly, for 1-2 minutes until the edges are translucent and the center remains opaque. This toasting step creates a shell around the grain so it doesn't turn to mush while slowly releasing starch.
Pour in the white wine. Stir constantly until the wine is fully absorbed by the rice.

Begin adding the warm broth, one ladle (about 0.5 cup) at a time. Stir frequently. Wait until the liquid is almost completely absorbed before adding the next ladle. The friction from stirring rubs the grains together, releasing the starch that creates the creamy sauce. Repeat this process for about 20-25 minutes. The rice is done when it is tender but still has a slight bite (al dente).

Remove the pot from the heat. This is crucial. Stir in the cooked mushrooms, vegan butter, and nutritional yeast. Vigorously stir the mixture for 30 seconds to emulsify the fats with the starch. This step guarantees the creamy mouthfeel without dairy. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Garnish with fresh parsley and serve immediately.

props.text:
Beginner-Friendly 6-Player Game Recommendations

Group Dynamics and Selection Criteria
These recommendations assume the group has little to no prior experience with modern hobby board games. The selections focus on high interaction, minimal downtime between turns, and rules that can be taught in under 5 minutes. The games selected bridge the gap between casual conversation and structured play, ensuring the 60-minute time limit is respected even with teaching time included.

Top Party and Deduction Picks

Option 1: Codenames | Team-based word association game | Party / 15 Minutes
The group splits into two teams, Red and Blue. Each team has a Spymaster who provides one-word clues linked to multiple cards on the table. The goal is for teammates to guess the correct words based on the clue without picking the opposing team's words or the instant-loss Assassin card. It encourages clever thinking and group discussion.
Action: [Button: View on BoardGameGeek] https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/178900/codenames

Option 2: Just One | Cooperative guessing game | Party / 20 Minutes
This is a fully cooperative game where everyone wins or loses together. One player is the guesser, and the other five write one-word clues to help them guess a specific word. The catch is that if any two players write the exact same clue, those clues are erased and the guesser never sees them. It forces players to be creative rather than obvious.
Action: [Button: View on BoardGameGeek] https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/254640/just-one

Option 3: Deception: Murder in Hong Kong | Crime-solving deduction game | Social Deduction / 20 Minutes
One player is secretly the Murderer, and another is the Forensic Scientist who knows the solution but can only communicate by placing markers on scene tiles (like Cause of Death: Suffocation). The remaining players are investigators trying to interpret these vague clues to identify the murderer and the weapon used. It is less aggressive than other lying games because the focus is on the evidence.
Action: [Button: View on BoardGameGeek] https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/156129/deception-murder-in-hong-kong

Option 4: The Resistance | Dystopian secret identity game | Social Deduction / 30 Minutes
Players are members of a resistance group trying to overthrow a government, but spies have infiltrated the ranks. In each round, a leader proposes a team to go on a mission. Everyone votes to approve the team. If the mission goes ahead, players on the team secretly choose to Support or Sabotage the mission. The goal is to deduce who the saboteurs are based on voting patterns and mission results.
Action: [Button: View on BoardGameGeek] https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/41114/the-resistance

Kyoto Family Trip Overview (April 5-7)

Visiting Kyoto in early April places you in the peak of spring season. While cherry blossoms (sakura) may be starting to flutter down by April 5-7, the city will be vibrant and busy. This itinerary balances the crowds by mixing popular historical sites with ample outdoor space for children. The schedule prioritizes locations with direct transit access or short taxi rides to strictly limit transit-to-destination walking to under 30 minutes.

Pacing and Transit Context

To accommodate children ages 8 and 10 and the walking constraints, this plan utilizes a "hub" approach where you visit one major area in the morning and one in the afternoon.

- Hiking Note: The hikes selected (Monkey Park and Fushimi Inari) are the activities themselves, not transit walks. Both have rest stops and safe paths.
- Weather Framework: Early April averages 10-20 degrees Celsius (50-68 F). Rain is possible, so indoor backups like the Railway Museum are included.

3-Day Itinerary: Temples & Trails

Day 1: Arashiyama Nature & Wildlife | Iwatayama Monkey Park (easy hike) and Bamboo Grove | West Kyoto
Start at JR Saga-Arashiyama Station. Walk 15 minutes to the Monkey Park entrance; the climb is an easy 20-minute trail with monkeys at the summit. Afterward, cross the Togetsukyo Bridge to the Bamboo Grove.
Action: [Button: Arashiyama Area Guide] https://kyoto.travel/en/areas/arashiyama.html

Day 2: Iconic Gates & Views | Fushimi Inari Shrine and Kiyomizu-dera | Southern & Eastern Kyoto
Morning at Fushimi Inari (JR Inari Station is immediately adjacent). The lower loop hike is gentle and features thousands of gates. Afternoon: Take a taxi to Kiyomizu-dera to avoid the steep approach walk.
Action: [Button: Fushimi Inari Maps] https://inari.jp/en/map/

Day 3: Gold Pavilion & Trains | Kinkaku-ji Temple and Kyoto Railway Museum | North & Central
Morning: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion). Access via taxi or direct bus to minimize walking. Afternoon: Kyoto Railway Museum (adjacent to Umekoji-Kyotonishi Station). Interactive and ideal for ages 8-10.
Action: [Button: Railway Museum Info] https://www.kyotorailwaymuseum.jp/en/

Families in Kyoto often prefer casual dining where noise levels are acceptable and menus are visual.
- Conveyor Belt Sushi (Kaitenzushi): "Kura Sushi" or "Sushiro" chains offer tablets for ordering and separate booths.
- Udon and Soba Noodles: "Omen" near Ginkaku-ji or Arashiyama offers dipping noodles that are fun for kids.
- Okonomiyaki: Savory pancakes where you can watch the food being cooked on a hotplate. "Donguri" is a family-friendly chain.
- Department Store Basements (Depachika): Located under Isetan (Kyoto Station) or Takashimaya. Great for picking up high-quality bento boxes for a picnic if restaurants are too crowded.

props.text: January is widely considered the peak travel season for both cities, but for very different reasons. Bangkok experiences its "cool" season, which is dry and sunny but still hot by global standards. Hanoi experiences a true winter, which is significantly cooler and often overcast with mist. For a walking tour, Hanoi offers much more comfortable temperatures, while Bangkok guarantees brighter photography conditions at the cost of heat exhaustion risks.

The following comparison relies on historical climate averages collected over the last 30 years. January weather patterns in Southeast Asia are generally stable, but short-term fluctuations (such as cold snaps in Hanoi or heatwaves in Bangkok) can occur. "Rainfall probability" here refers to the likelihood of measurable precipitation days, though intensity varies (Bangkok rain is rare/short; Hanoi rain is often a persistent light drizzle).
